hypotheses.statement: Vertical clipping: an element around the yellow note has a fixed height or max-height with overflow:hidden. At 390px the sentence wraps onto more lines than the box can hold, so the lower lines are cut off.
hypotheses.prediction: At 390x844: rect.height is much smaller than the estimated height (heightRatio < ~0.75), or an ancestor rect ends above the estimated text bottom (clipsBottom = true). Pixel rows near the bottom of the text have little or no dark ink, and the last-fragment checks show it exists in the DOM. At 1440x900 none of this shows (heightRatio ≈ 1, no clipsBottom).
hypotheses.falsifier: At 390x844 every pixel row inside the text rect has ink, heightRatio is ≥ ~0.85 and no ancestor ends above the needed text bottom. H1 is rejected.

hypotheses.statement: Horizontal overflow: the note's text does not wrap (white-space:nowrap, a fixed or min width, or text-overflow:ellipsis). At 390px the line runs past the right edge of its container or the viewport.
hypotheses.prediction: At 390x844: the text rect is about one line tall (rectLines ≈ 1), and rightOverflow > 0 or an ancestor ends left of the text's right edge (clipsRight = true). The visible part has ink from left to right. The end fragments are still in the DOM. At 1440x900, rightOverflow ≤ 0.
hypotheses.falsifier: At 390x844 the text rect sits inside both the viewport and every ancestor (rightOverflow ≤ 0, no clipsRight) and covers several lines. H2 is rejected.

hypotheses.statement: Occlusion: another painted element, such as a sticky bar, a positioned sibling, a banner or the parent's pseudo-element, sits on top of the later part of the sentence in the narrow layout.
hypotheses.prediction: At 390x844: at sample points in the later rows or columns of the text rect, the topmost stack entry is not the text element (selfDepth > 0, and the top entry is often positioned with an opaque background). At those cells the pixel ink drops to about 0 while earlier cells have ink. At 1440x900, selfDepth is 0 at all points.
hypotheses.falsifier: At 390x844 the text element (or a descendant carrying the same text) is topmost (selfDepth 0) at every in-rect sample point, and ink is present in all cells. H3 is rejected.

probe.question: For packet.target at 1440x900 and 390x844: does the note's text rect fit its ancestors and the viewport? What is topmost at points across the rect, row by row? Is there dark ink in every row and column cell inside the rect? Is the end of the sentence present in the DOM at all?
probe.falsifier: If, at 390x844, every row and column cell inside the text rect has ink, the text element is topmost everywhere, nothing overflows horizontally or vertically, and the estimated line count is met, then H1, H2 and H3 are all rejected for this version. The symptom is then either absent on this version or has a cause outside these three, such as truncated text content.
controls: The same probe at 1440x900 serves as the within-version baseline. The user reports the laptop view is fine, so the numbers there should look normal.
Counts for the beginning, middle and end fragments separate 'text missing from the DOM' (JS or content truncation) from 'present but not rendered'.
Ink in the first row and left cell is a positive control: rendered text on a yellow background gives below[150] > 0.
A strip just below the text rect shows whether the text overflows visibly or something else sits there.
Each stack entry is compared with the text element's own tag, class and rect (selfDepth), not just its computed style.
The page is scrolled so the note is near the top of the viewport, and the text is found again afterwards, so all coordinates are in the current viewport.
limitations: Line height and line count are estimates (1.4×font-size and about 0.5em per character), so heightRatio is approximate and only indicative near 1.
The broker does not expose overflow, white-space, height or max-height. Clipping is inferred from rects, stacks and pixels, not read directly.

Pseudo-elements are not separate stack entries. An overlay drawn by ::before or ::after appears as its host element, and selfDepth may be 0 for a parent's ::after only when the host is the text element itself.
Pixels can only be captured inside the viewport. Text past the right edge or below the fold cannot be photographed, only shown by geometry.
If the sentence is split across several text nodes or inline elements, the element found contains only part of it. All fragment counts are reported, but the rect covers that part only.
The ink threshold (<150 grey) assumes dark text on a light or yellow background.
The probe runs only on packet.target. Comparing the two versions means running it once for each target.
